rules.quote: In all mathematical expressions, write numbers as numerals.
rules.violation_condition: a number written as a word rather than a numeral in a mathematical expression
when: This applies even when you use words to explain a relationship between the numbers.
rules.why: Specific, actionable mechanical rule on expressing numbers in mathematical expressions.

covers.quote: Use code, not punctuation, for mathematical symbols
Always use the correct code for mathematical symbols
Don't use:
the minus symbol on the numerical keypad
an en dash (–)
a hyphen (-).

examples.note: Using the Unicode character for minus.
Using a keyboard hyphen instead of the mathematical minus symbol.

rules.quote: Don’t use punctuation marks (such as a dash) instead of a symbol.
rules.violation_condition: a punctuation mark such as a hyphen or dash used instead of the mathematical operator symbol (such as a minus sign)
when: When writing mathematical expressions with operators and relations.
rules.why: G-2, G-4: Consolidated general requirement and specific minus punctuation prohibitions into one rule.

covers.quote: Don’t use a symbol or a space for ratios
Ratios don’t have a space around the colon.

examples.note: Ratio with no spaces around the colon.
Ratio with spaces around the colon.

rules.quote: Ratios don’t have a space around the colon.
rules.violation_condition: a space (breaking or non-breaking) placed immediately before or after a colon used to express a ratio
when: In expressions showing ratios using a colon.
rules.why: Clear, automatable spacing constraint for ratio colons.

covers.quote: To show addition, use non-breaking spaces around the plus symbol.
To show subtraction, use non-breaking spaces around the minus symbol.
Use non-breaking spaces around the division symbol.
Use non-breaking spaces around the multiplication symbol.
When research shows that users need the symbols, use non-breaking spaces between the symbol and numbers.
When research shows that users need the symbols (and algebraic expressions), use non-breaking spaces.
Put a non-breaking space around the equals symbol and around all operators except for the division slash – it is unspaced.

examples.note: Addition with non-breaking spaces around plus.
Addition without spaces around plus.
Subtraction with non-breaking spaces around minus.
Subtraction without spaces around minus.
Equation with non-breaking spaces around plus and equals.
Equation lacking non-breaking spaces around operators and equals.

rules.quote: Insert a non-breaking space between numbers, letters and the symbol for an operator or a relation.
rules.violation_condition: an operator, relation, or equals sign in a mathematical expression lacking a non-breaking space on either side, or using an unspaced or breaking space format
when: Except when the symbol modifies a single value (such as a positive or negative sign).
Except for the division slash, which is unspaced (or may take narrow no-break or thin spaces).
rules.why: G-1, G-2: Consolidated overarching non-breaking space rule for all mathematical operators and relations across the page.

covers.quote: Don’t use a space if a symbol modifies a value
To show a positive value, write the number after the plus symbol without a space.
To show a negative value, write the number after the minus symbol without a space.
When the symbol acts as a mathematical adjective, there is no space between the symbol and the character it modifies.

examples.note: Positive value with no space after plus.
Positive value with non-breaking space after plus.
Negative value with no space after minus.
Negative value with space after minus.

rules.quote: Symbols that modify a value rather than show an operation or a relationship, do not need a space.
rules.violation_condition: a space appearing between a modifying mathematical symbol (such as positive + or negative −) and the number or character it modifies
when: When the symbol acts to show a positive or negative value rather than an operation.
rules.why: G-2, G-4: Consolidated specific instructions against spacing modifying symbols (adjectival symbols).

rules.quote: Write variables in italics. Do not italicise other elements.
rules.violation_condition: a variable in a mathematical expression not written in italics, or a non-variable element (such as an operator or numeral) written in italics
when: In mathematical expressions containing variables.
rules.why: Clear typographical rule regarding mathematical variables.

covers.quote: Use the mathematical symbol for the multiplication (×).

rules.violation_condition: the Latin letter 'x' or 'X' used instead of the multiplication symbol (×)
when: When indicating mathematical multiplication.
rules.why: Distinct character substitution violation condition specifically targeting the letter 'x'.

covers.quote: The asterisk has other meanings in algebra, so only use it for multiplication if users will understand what you mean.

examples.note: Multiplication symbol used.
Multiplication dot used in general content.
Asterisk used for multiplication.

rules.quote: Use the multiplication symbol in general content, not the dot operator.
rules.violation_condition: the dot operator (⋅ or ·) or asterisk (*) used for multiplication in general content
when: In general content.
rules.why: G-2: Covers alternative multiplication notation (dot operator and asterisk).

rules.quote: Programming languages use the symbols ‘>=’ and ‘<=’ for these relationships. Don’t use them in your content, they are not mathematical notation.
rules.violation_condition: the ASCII programming constructs '>=' or '<=' used instead of '≥' or '≤'
rules.why: Direct, actionable syntax prohibition.
